description: 5 exemplars (one German) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-29 under road-to-a-correction-that-is-heard step 2.3, which made instruction-file prose a conflict source next to the configs and so brought the skill into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the skill's own 'When to use': the enforced style before writing code, the commit convention, a standards card while orienting, and a repeated correction that may contradict the config. Near-misses are neighbours that also read a project but are someone else's job: the concrete shape of a class or schema (source-discovery), turning a recurring mistake into a rule or skill (learning-to-rule-or-skill), and running the formatter itself (quality-tools). Counterexamples guard the words 'standard' and 'config': an industry-standard question and a server configuration request.

queries.q: before I touch this repo — what indent, line length and quote style does it actually enforce?
what commit message format does this project expect? check the tooling, don't guess
write a short standards card for this repo from its eslint and prettier config so the next agent doesn't re-derive it
the user keeps telling me to use tabs but I'm not sure what the editorconfig says — which one wins?
welche Import-Reihenfolge und Namenskonventionen erzwingt dieses Projekt laut seiner Konfiguration?
which columns does the orders table have and what does the OrderResource return?
queries.note: the concrete shape of code, read fresh → source-discovery

queries.q: we forgot the same lint rule three times this week — turn it into something durable
queries.note: a recurring lesson to encode → learning-to-rule-or-skill

queries.q: run the formatter and fix whatever phpstan complains about
queries.note: running the tools, not deriving the standard → quality-tools

queries.q: is OAuth 2.1 already an industry standard or still a draft?
configure nginx to proxy websocket connections to port 6001
queries.note: says config, asks for server configuration rather than a coding standard
